summary: Completed the bounded architecture/documentation review of the proposed XTK Systems office deployment. No supported actionable findings were identified. The plan describes available runtime adapters accurately, identifies its missing preflight and PostgreSQL/local-file recovery preparation, and keeps provisioning, capacity, and production admission conditional.
coverage: Bound to source HEAD e3149dd11f1fa67b4955b4eec3d998aa82be284e and docs/live-deployment-plan.md SHA256 1795013e045861e7b79c1560b30b8a12067ccf128367b7e462d5f12aa3b9a553. All eleven file digests in plan.json were checked and match.

Read AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .codex-context/system.json, project.md and workflow.md; read docs-writer and adversarial-review skill contracts and review schema. No nested instruction files were found under docs or .codex-context.
Reviewed the complete revised deployment plan, docs/pilot-acceptance.md and the applicable operational upgrade, local-backup, PostgreSQL-recovery, and retention guidance in docs/operations.md.

Inspected compose.yaml and Dockerfile: the supplied stack is development/dev-sign-in/SQLite/local-files; the image runs as node. The plan correctly requires separate production packaging, persistent volume ownership, and explicit secret-to-environment injection.

Inspected storage/index.ts, postgres.ts, sqlite.ts and blobs/index.ts. SQL backend and blob backend selection are independent, supporting one PostgreSQL/local-file application instance. PostgreSQL is documented in source as the production backend; additional replicas cannot share independent local artifact roots.

Inspected pilot-preflight.ts and local-backup.ts: preflight hard-requires PostgreSQL/S3, and local backup uses SQLite-specific snapshots and artifact reference validation. The office profile and coordinated PostgreSQL/local-files restore are accurately identified as unimplemented preparation.

Cross-checked auth/config.ts, startup.ts, context.ts, repo-scan.ts, agent mode and targeted auth service/http references for the plan settings, OIDC callback and scopes. Reviewed scripts/pilot-rehearsal.mjs and resources.mjs references for PostgreSQL 17, S3 recovery and limits of local rehearsal evidence.

Checked official Microsoft Ubuntu Hyper-V support and Docker Ubuntu Engine documentation: Ubuntu 24.04 is documented, while actual Windows Server version and host headroom remain required inventory inputs.

Checked official Google OAuth audience/consent documentation and Cloudflare Tunnel/Access documentation for the proposed identity and optional remote-access path. Connector-side Access validation and Access-before-route sequencing are documented capabilities.

Checked PostgreSQL 17 pg_dump/pg_restore documentation against coordinated stopped-writer capture, separate cluster roles/configuration custody, compatible custom-format archive, fresh restore targets and fail-on-error requirements.
limitations: This is a source/documentation review, not a deployment acceptance or performance result. No builds, tests, service/container/VM operations, credential access, provider account calls or live infrastructure changes were performed.

Application-security reassessment, exploit reproduction and retrying the previous interrupted security work were outside this assignment. Existing F01-F11/T01 findings and the previous release hold are unchanged.

Physical host identity, Windows Server versions, support state, free CPU/RAM/storage under VDI load, network route, UPS, backup destination and recovery objectives are unverified. Proposed VM allocations are not minimum requirements or measured capacity.

Production Compose, the office preflight profile, secret injection, ingress/certificate setup, backup scheduling and the PostgreSQL/local-file recovery runbook remain future work explicitly gated in the plan. No exact-topology recovery, real Google login or VDI browser acceptance was executed.

The existing pilot worksheet is a generic hosted/PostgreSQL-object-storage template. Office-specific host, filesystem, recovery and acceptance evidence will need to be recorded during the planned preparation and staging work.
Vendor documentation was read publicly; tenant-specific service configuration, subscription entitlements and operational availability were not inspected.
